items.title: Kent Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: if you have a Kenny Barron or if you have a Wynton Marsalis or whoever you have, a Terence Blanchard or whoever you have on your staff as part of your faculty people are attracted to that.

ctx.x: Well I’m curious if you ran into any — even teaching at NOCCA and that kind of thing, did you run into any academia political type things once you get into education?

Well actually yea, I quit NOCCA and now I’m starting like another arts-based school, well I should say, I’m sorry, I resigned. That’s politically more correct. And actually Alvin Batiste took my place when I left NOCCA. And I feel like there’s two things that should happen when you talk about academia. Part of it is that when you get into academia or in a situation where you can teach you should try to practice more and study more and play more. Even though your time is dedicated to obviously teaching. Now the…

this because I heard this the other night or I read about this or this is something that you may find interesting because you’re interested in this. You know what I mean? To me that’s what’s important. Not that you can think of another class to offer because it sounds good in your course offerings, but to really come up with people who really are knowledgeable.
